---
title: "Notebook"
subtitle: "The exploratory notebook is documentation, not a build step"
toc: true
---

The original exploration lives in
[`eprtr_analysis.ipynb`](https://github.com/pilzsa/eprtr_usetox/blob/main/eprtr_analysis.ipynb)
at the repository root: 143 cells that load the E-PRTR air and water tables,
map EC/CAS numbers, attach the IARC, CLP, SVHC, EPA HAP and WFD lists, merge the
IED permit table, and sketch the sector questions that became this atlas.

It is **not executed when the site is built**, for three reasons:

1. It uses absolute paths to the local EEA download (the CSVs are not in git).
2. It needs GDAL for the LAU join, which the site build does not require.
3. Its outputs are exploratory figures; the site's numbers must come from the
   reproducible scripts in `analysis/`, not from notebook state.

Everything the notebook established is implemented, with tests against the
published totals, in:

| Notebook section | Pipeline counterpart |
|:--|:--|
| Data check, upload, cleaning, merging | `analysis/build_dataset.py` |
| EC/CAS matching and official lists | `analysis/hazard_rules.py` |
| Facility details and IED merge | `analysis/build_permits.py` |
| USEtox availability | not used in the atlas (mass ≠ toxicity) |
| Sector focus (A/B) | kept as context, not as a filter |

## Re-running it

```bash
pip install pandas matplotlib openpyxl emipy
jupyter lab eprtr_analysis.ipynb
```

The notebook assumes the EEA files at the paths it prints in its first code
cell. Re-running it is useful for exploring new questions; it is not needed to
rebuild the site.

::: {.callout-note}
The notebook's USEtox section is deliberately not carried into the site. USEtox
characterisation factors answer "how toxic is a kilogram if it reaches a
receptor", which is a different question from "what did the facility report".
Mixing the two would hide the assumptions behind a single score; the atlas
keeps reported mass, hazard screening and population exposure separate.
:::
